messages.subject: methylation context in birds
parts:
I have CHH, CpH and CpG contexts in my samples.  It looks like I would need to filter  each sample for each context and run them separately?  I'm guessing it isn't preferable to leave them lumped together in 1 file?  Also, is there a way to leave the context in the input file and let methylkit identify them during the analysis?  I currently am using a methyl call input file (chr.base, chr, base, strand, coverage, freq C, freq T).

Thansk

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] methylation context in birds
parts:
You need to separate the files for each context. I am not sure it makes sense biologically to look at all the contexts at the same time. CpG context is special in certain species. 
If you really want to pile everything up together and do the analysis, you can. But you can not use destrand=TRUE in the unite() function.

In addition, if you know your way around BSgenome package, you can filter the Cs based on their context later on. Basically, you need to find the locations of all Cs in different contexts for the whole genome. And use that location information to filter methylKit objects to different contexts. But I think it is best to do it beforehand. 

Best,
Altuna
